findings.title: Resolved manifest does not activate or resolve the claimed 13 prompts
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 2: “Resolved manifest exists, contains exactly 13 activated prompts (P00, P00A, P01–P10)”
findings.trigger: The manifest is used to dispatch any downstream prompt P01–P10.
findings.consequence: Eleven entries remain `template_requires_resolution`, and eight entries reference nonexistent prompt files, so the claimed resolved 13-prompt execution set cannot be executed.
findings.evidence: `prompt_manifest.resolved.v1.yaml` marks P01–P10/P02S as `template_requires_resolution`. Its P03–P10 paths use nonexistent filenames such as `P03_source_relocation.prompt.v3.yaml`; the repository instead contains differently named templates such as `P03_source_move.prompt.v3.yaml`.

findings.title: P02S does not own the live structured-file edits
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 4 pass condition: “P02S owns all structured file edits”
findings.trigger: A downstream phase applies a TOML, JSON, or YAML transformation to a live repository file.
findings.consequence: The live edit is owned and applied outside P02S, contradicting the required exclusive structured-file ownership and preventing the stated ownership gate from passing.
findings.evidence: The manifest assigns P02S only `toml_json_yaml_codemod_tooling`. The P02S prompt explicitly says, “Do not edit live TOML/JSON/YAML files; downstream owners apply the proven codemod only to mutation units allocated by the resolved manifest.”

observations: The checkpoint’s mutation-unit accounting is internally confusing: the displayed P01–P10 allocation sums to 22, while 24 is reached only by also counting P00 and P00A; a later section separately claims 26 by adding two infrastructure units.

The rollback block includes `git checkout HEAD -- plans_internal/refactor_repo/`, which is broader than removing only the six newly created P00A artifacts and could discard unrelated planning changes.
reasoning: I independently confirmed the P00 verdict state, inventory completeness, stated inventory and baseline hashes, clean authorization boundary, and successful P00A schema validation. Acceptance criteria 1–20 are each represented once in the checkpoint map, including Criterion 20 under P08. The two surviving findings directly defeat Criteria 2 and 4 at blocker severity; the remaining concerns were retained only as non-blocking observations.
